feed.title: AI · RAG, Embeddings & Vectors — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Raven
entry.summary: A memory-first agent harness centred on cross-session learning and refining its own configuration.

entry.title: Atlas Vector Search
entry.summary: The vector index sits beside your documents, removing the copy-and-sync burden of a separate store. Atlas only — it is not in a self-managed MongoDB.

entry.title: BGE Modelleri
entry.summary: The most widely used family of open embedding models. It sits close to paid APIs on the MTEB leaderboard and most releases are MIT, so commercial use is unblocked.

entry.title: Chroma
entry.summary: Runs embedded in your application with no server process — usable straight after `pip install`. Fastest for a prototype; at production scale you will hand off to something else.

entry.title: Cohere Embed
entry.summary: Represents 100+ languages in one vector space, so a Turkish query can retrieve an English document. Taking separate input types for query and document lifts match quality.

entry.title: Elasticsearch
entry.summary: Combines BM25 keyword search with vector search in a single query and fuses the results with RRF. That keyword half is exactly what pure vector databases lack.

entry.title: GraphRAG
entry.summary: Extracts entities and relations into a knowledge graph, then builds community summaries. Corpus-wide questions like “what are the main themes here” cannot be answered by chunk retrieval; this exists for those.

entry.title: Haystack
entry.summary: You wire components together explicitly, so what happens at each stage stays readable. When debugging, that transparency is a visible win over LangChain’s implicit flow.

entry.title: LangGraph Memory
entry.summary: The concept page separating short-term memory (in-thread state) from long-term (a cross-thread store), and when each applies.

entry.title: Letta
entry.summary: The productised form of the MemGPT research. It manages the context window like an operating system, keeping hot state in the window and paging the rest to external storage.

entry.title: LlamaIndex
entry.summary: Makes each stage — loading, chunking, indexing, querying — independently swappable. Not a general-purpose framework: it is built for someone tuning a retrieval pipeline.

entry.title: Mem0
entry.summary: Stores facts extracted from conversation, updates contradictions and drops the irrelevant. A layer that decides what is worth remembering instead of accumulating raw history.

entry.title: Mem0 (kaynak)
entry.summary: The self-hostable version of Mem0. The Embedchain project was merged into this repository, so older Embedchain links land here.

entry.title: Milvus
entry.summary: A distributed architecture separating storage from compute, built for billion-scale collections. It wants Kubernetes; on a small project the setup cost exceeds the gain.

entry.title: Neo4j
entry.summary: Relationships are first-class data, not foreign keys. Multi-hop traversals in Cypher are both shorter and faster than the nested JOINs the same question needs in SQL.

entry.title: OpenAI Embeddings
entry.summary: Reference for the text-embedding-3 family — dimensions, pricing, usage. Matryoshka support lets you truncate vector dimensions on demand and cut storage cost.

entry.title: pgvector
entry.summary: An extension adding a vector type plus HNSW and IVFFlat indexes to PostgreSQL. Keeping vectors in the same transaction as relational data is worth a lot against running a second system.

entry.title: Pinecone
entry.summary: A fully managed vector database whose serverless tier removes capacity planning. The lowest operational burden here, at the cost of control over where the data sits.

entry.title: PostgreSQL
entry.summary: With JSONB, full-text search and pgvector it now does the work of three separate systems. Early on, that simplifies architecture considerably.

entry.title: Qdrant
entry.summary: Written in Rust, executing heavy metadata filtering alongside the vector search itself. Its low memory footprint lets a small VPS carry a serious collection.

entry.title: Ragas
entry.summary: A metrics library for RAG pipelines, including metrics that work without reference answers. It can generate a synthetic test set so evaluation runs in CI.

entry.title: RAGFlow
entry.summary: Built on deep document parsing: it recognises complex PDF layouts, tables and figures before chunking. Not a library but a full service you stand up with Docker.

entry.title: Redis
entry.summary: An in-memory data structure store, used on the AI side for session state, rate-limit counters and response caching. Vector search arrives as a module.

entry.title: Sentence Transformers
entry.summary: The standard Python library for producing embeddings. Models run locally, data stays put and there is no API bill; in exchange GPU and memory management are yours.

entry.title: TruLens
entry.summary: Measures the RAG triad — context relevance, groundedness, answer relevance. Measuring them separately is what tells you whether the failure sits in retrieval or generation.

entry.title: Unstructured
entry.summary: Reduces PDF, DOCX, HTML, email and slides to a shared document-element model. This first step is where RAG pipelines lose the most time and break most often.

entry.title: Vertex AI Embeddings
entry.summary: The embedding service inside GCP. If your data sits in BigQuery, generating vectors within the same boundary makes sense for both egress cost and data residency.

entry.title: Voyage AI
entry.summary: Embedding models trained separately for law, code and finance. It claims to beat general-purpose models inside those domains — a claim worth testing on your own data.

entry.title: Weaviate
entry.summary: Can host embedding generation as a module, so you write raw text without standing up a separate embedding step. Its query interface is GraphQL.

entry.title: Zep
entry.summary: Maintains a temporal knowledge graph, recording when a fact held and when it was invalidated. Flat vector memory cannot make that distinction.

entry.title: Graphify
entry.summary: Walks a codebase via AST analysis and folds in docs, SQL schemas and PDFs to build a queryable graph. Designed to feed context to a coding agent.
